$comment: Hand-authored from Robot.configureBindings(). This is the SOURCE OF TRUTH for the controls pages. Auto-generating it from the Java would be misleading: the LT/RT behaviour lives inside Commands.either(...) conditions, so the trigger expression alone understates what the robot does. The app's own drift check (scripts/check-drift.mjs, surfaced at /api/drift and in the page banner) verifies every pilot.X / operator.X referenced in configureBindings() appears here and vice versa. It reports; it never fails a build.

controllers.name: Pilot
notes: Stick deadzone 0.10, exponential curve 3.0 on both sticks. Stick scalars are overwritten at runtime from the swerve's max speeds.

Driving is NOT a binding. Swerve has no default command; it reads the pilot sticks directly in calculateSpeedsBasedOnJoystickInputs() (Swerve.java:346-348), so drive never appears in configureBindings().

bindings.detail: Only when RT is not already held. Enters INTAKE_FUEL.
Only when LT is not already held. Enters LAUNCH_WITH_SQUEEZE.
Releasing RT restores the default feed target. If LT is still held it falls back to INTAKE_FUEL instead of idling.
Only when RT is held: releasing LT enters LAUNCH_WITH_SQUEEZE_WITH_NO_DELAY, skipping the squeeze wait.
Turret and hood aim at the hub without feeding. On release it idles unless already launching.
Runs everything backwards to clear a stuck ball. Idles on release.
Everything backwards except the intake kicker, which keeps running forward. Idles on release.
Re-homes the intake extension. Requires LB NOT held, since LB+Select is the vision reset.

controllers.name: Operator
notes: Trigger deadzone 0.0; everything else at Gamepad.Config defaults.

The D-pad is the shot-outcome log. Every press is written to ShotCalc/Trim/* with the distance of the burst it is judging, which is why there are no separate short/made/long buttons: a made shot is the absence of a press. See docs/tools/shot-log.md.

bindings.detail: Nudges ShotCalculator's HOOD_ANGLE_OFFSET up, which is also how the operator says the last burst fell short: the press is logged as ShotCalc/Trim/* with Verdict=Short and paired with the most recent shot record. Saved to the rio with WPILib Preferences on every press, so it survives a redeploy AND a power cycle. A non-zero trim is printed at boot; Start+Select zeroes both. Capped at +/-10 deg. Works while disabled.

Shots going long? Come down. Logged as ShotCalc/Trim/* with Verdict=Long and paired with the most recent shot record, which is what makes a practice session a dataset. Saved to the rio with WPILib Preferences on every press, so it survives a redeploy AND a power cycle. A non-zero trim is printed at boot; Start+Select zeroes both. Capped at +/-10 deg. Works while disabled.

Nudges TURRET_ANGLE_OFFSET counter-clockwise; logged with Verdict=MissedCW, meaning the ball landed clockwise of the target. Saved to the rio with WPILib Preferences on every press, so it survives a redeploy AND a power cycle. A non-zero trim is printed at boot; Start+Select zeroes both. Capped at +/-10 deg. Works while disabled.

Nudges TURRET_ANGLE_OFFSET clockwise; logged with Verdict=MissedCCW. Saved to the rio with WPILib Preferences on every press, so it survives a redeploy AND a power cycle. A non-zero trim is printed at boot; Start+Select zeroes both. Capped at +/-10 deg. Works while disabled.
HELD, not pressed. Bypasses every shot-readiness gate and feeds anyway. This is not an onTrue binding — the trigger is handed to SuperStructure.setFeedOverride() as a live condition.
Releasing either bumper restores the default feed target.

bindings.action: Reset both shot trims to zero
bindings.detail: Clears the hood and turret trims and the values stored on the rio. Needed because the trims now persist across a power cycle: without this, a trim dialled in against a shop ceiling last week would silently apply at the next event and the only way out would be a redeploy. Works in all modes; a chord of the two buttons nothing else uses.
Same as pilot A.

Point the turret away from the intake BY HAND first, then press. The turret no longer zeroes itself on code start, so this is how the zero gets set. Check Turret/PositionDegrees reads near 0 afterwards.
